newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jewish settlers demonstrate in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Jewish settlers demonstrate in Hebron.

text.p: Hundreds of Jewish settlers demonstrated in the West Bank town of Hebron on Saturday against its future partial handover to Palestinian rule, Israeli security sources and Palestinian witnesses said.
The settlers blocked a road between Palestinian neighbourhoods in Hebron and the adjacent Jewish settlement of Kiryat Arba, security sources said.
The Israeli army said it was checking the report. Police spokesmen were not immediately available to comment.

Palestinian witnesses who arrived on the scene after the demonstration began said the numbers had thinned to about 100 settlers. They said soldiers ringed the demonstrators and prevented them from approaching Palestinians.
They said the demonstrators chanted: "We don't want Arabs" and "Don't bring (Palestinian) rifles to Hebron".
Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation began talks this week on implementing a deal to redeploy Israeli troops in Hebron signed by Israel's previous centre-left government.
Palestinians accuse Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of trying to rewrite the deal signed in Washington under the auspices of President Bill Clinton.
Netanyahu, who took office in June, says security measures must be increased for the 400 settlers who live in the midst of the 100,000 Palestinians in Hebron. Some 5,500 settlers live in Kiryat Arba.
Israel was to have redeployed in March but the previous government delayed the move in the wake of Islamic militant suicide bombings that killed 59 people in Israel in March and February.

Talks on implementing it were decided on at an emergency Washington summit after fierce Palestinian-Israeli clashes last month spurred by Israel's opening of a second entrance to a tourist tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem. Sixty Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed in the fighting.

Early on Saturday a leader of the outlawed anti-Arab Kach movement who lives in Hebron warned of an explosion of violence if the redeployment were carried out. Settler Baruch Merzel said there were groups organising against the introduction of Palestinian police into Hebron under the deal.
"We have a record of reaction to Arab provocations. We will not go like a herd of sheep to slaughter even if the government is a right-wing government," Merzel told Israel Radio.

Hebron is a flashpoint of Jewish-Arab violence. In February 1994 a settler from Kiryat Arba shot dead 29 Arabs at prayer in a Hebron mosque. He was beaten to death by survivors. In 1929 Arabs massacred about 60 Jews in Hebron.
